newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's OCP firm signs $30 mln deal with Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's OCP firm signs $30 mln deal with Brazil.

text.p: Morocco's phosphates giant Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) has signed a $30 million a year deal with Brazil's Trevo group to expand its activities in South America, a spokesman said on Monday.

"The deal, which was recently signed with Brazilian Trevo group, will generate an annual receipt of $30 million...It is aimed also at expanding OCP's activity in Brazil and South America in general," the OCP spokesman said.
State-owned OCP will provide the Trevo group with "important quantities" of phosphate by-products each year to produce fertilisers, he said but declined to give details.
The private Trevo group, which was established in 1930, produces 1.0 million tonnes of composed fertilisers a year, including superphosphate products, he added.
The world's main phosphates exporter, OCP's shipments of phosphates and by-products in 1995 totalled 10 billion dirhams ($1.06 billion).
Updated figures were not immediately available.
